idiom_name: query function returning a new value + segregated command methods
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: split each model operation into a query that returns a value and writes nothing observable, and a command that changes state and returns no domain information. Push the complex part of a rule into immutable values so that composing rules cannot make one rule alter what the next one sees; pass every dependency the computation needs (clock, identifiers, configuration) as an explicit input instead of reading ambient state. Copy-on-update is the default realization; in-place mutation is a deliberate, local exception that the API names. Where the language cannot enforce read-only passing, the guarantee lives in the name, the documentation and the review, so keep the command set small and visible.
code_sketch:
# query: result from inputs only
price = price_for(basket, rate_card, today)
# command: state change, no domain result
account.post(amount)
# read-after-write is the caller's job
balance = account.balance()
pitfalls: A query that lazily loads, logs or caches in a field is a command wearing a query's name.
Reading ambient state (clock, locale, singleton config) inside the computation voids the guarantee without changing the signature.
Memoizing or parallelising an operation that is not actually pure turns a borrowed guarantee into a defect generator.

Wrong move: mutating the previous state or its nested objects inside a reducer or component that is supposed to be pure -> reference-comparing consumers (memoized selectors, React Redux useSelector, DevTools time-travel replay) never see the change or replay to the wrong state -> always build and return a new object and leave every input untouched.

Wrong move: calling Date.now(), Math.random() or a singleton inside a nominally pure reducer -> replaying the same action log twice yields different states, so undo/redo and record-replay tests silently diverge -> inject the clock and the randomness source from outside and pass them in as data.
